cost_model.borrow_source: B22G tier 'etb_general_collateral': 0.33%/yr. median IBKR indicative fee across 14 ETB names in this universe. Sources: Alpaca /v2/assets borrow_status for the traded account (complete over the universe) and Interactive Brokers' shortable-securities feed for the rate. AVAILABILITY, STATED CORRECTLY (a rate cannot express it, but the earlier wording overstated it): 8 of the 52 names the ORB rule ACTUALLY screened are hard-to-borrow and NOT SHORTABLE AT ALPACA (15.4%) -- not 36 of 100, which is the size of the screen INPUT rather than of the traded universe. NOT SHORTABLE AT ALPACA IS NOT 'unborrowable at any price': 7 of the 11 hard-to-borrow names with an obtainable IBKR rate have shares AVAILABLE to borrow there, at 2.32%-259.96%/yr -- expensive, not impossible, and a COST at another broker rather than a constraint. Of the 227 short signals in the B22B sample, 39 are in names Alpaca will not short, and 38 of those 39 are LEVERAGED or INVERSE ETPs (MSTU, SOXL, SOXS, SQQQ, TSLL) -- an Alpaca PRODUCT restriction, not borrow scarcity; exactly 1 is an ordinary common stock (ONDS). A strategy with a short leg must still handle availability as a constraint rather than a cost, but the constraint is mostly 'this broker does not lend leveraged ETPs', which a universe filter or another broker removes.
